readings: Using `player_college`, count each college's players as the number of rows (records) per `college_id`, with rows lacking a college_id treated as one group. Find the colleges whose row count is strictly above the average row count across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) those colleges' average row count; (2) the average of each one's row count as a fraction of the total row count across all colleges; and (3) the average amount by which their row counts exceed the all-college average. Do not round.

Using `player_college`, count each college's players as the number of distinct `player_id` values per `college_id`, so a player with several year records at one college counts once, with rows lacking a college_id treated as one group. Find the colleges whose distinct-player count is strictly above the average distinct-player count across all colleges. Return a single row with: (1) those colleges' average distinct-player count; (2) the average of each one's distinct-player count as a fraction of the total of all colleges' distinct-player counts; and (3) the average amount by which their counts exceed the all-college average. Do not round.
queries:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM player_college
  GROUP BY college_id
),
s AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS a, SUM(cnt) AS t
  FROM c
)
SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count,
       AVG(c.cnt * 1.0 / s.t) AS avg_fraction_of_total,
       AVG(c.cnt - s.a) AS avg_excess_over_average
FROM c, s
WHERE c.cnt > s.a;

WITH c AS (
  SELECT college_id, COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) AS cnt
  FROM player_college
  GROUP BY college_id
),
s AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS a, SUM(cnt) AS t
  FROM c
)
SELECT AVG(c.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_distinct_players,
       AVG(c.cnt * 1.0 / s.t) AS avg_fraction_of_total,
       AVG(c.cnt - s.a) AS avg_excess_over_average
FROM c, s
WHERE c.cnt > s.a
